ageing_relevance.rationale: High ageing/senescence literature share, UniProt role in cellular senescence, associations with several age-related diseases, and a GrimAge component. Disease association scores are modest.

evidence.value: One of seven plasma proteins whose DNA-methylation surrogates make up GrimAge, the mortality clock that was +4.3 years older in schizophrenia in part 1 of this project (an effect explained by smoking). The surrogates are methylation estimates, not measured protein levels.

background_knowledge: Human SERPINE1 loss-of-function mutation in Amish is associated with longer lifespan and protection from diabetes (Khan 2017).
PAI-1 inhibition reduces senescence in mouse models.

mechanism.rationale: Well-characterised inhibitor of tPA/uPA with a defined role in senescence. Lowering PAI-1 is the clear direction, although the senescence pathway is pleiotropic.

evidence.value: Serine protease inhibitor... primary inhibitor of tissue-type plasminogen activator (PLAT) and urokinase-type plasminogen activator (PLAU)... involved in cellular and replicative senescence

background_knowledge: PAI-1 is a SASP component and p53 target that promotes senescence.

tractability.rationale: Small molecule tractability includes advanced clinical stage, ligand-bound structure and high-quality pocket. The protein is secreted, so antibodies are also feasible. No approved drug.

safety.rationale: Open Targets lists 2 liabilities, including osteonecrosis. Congenital deficiency causes abnormal bleeding, so inhibition carries a bleeding risk.

value: congenital plasminogen activator inhibitor type 1 deficiency (0.684)

background_knowledge: Human PAI-1 deficiency causes a mild-to-moderate bleeding diathesis, which is usually manageable.

clinical_precedence.rationale: Only one drug, aleplasinin, has reached the clinic, and its maximum stage is Phase 1.

assessment.summary: SERPINE1 (PAI-1) is a secreted inhibitor of tPA/uPA and a senescence-associated factor. About 21% of its papers concern ageing, and it is linked to cardiovascular, metabolic and neurodegenerative disease and to GrimAge. Inhibition is the likely direction for slowing ageing. It is tractable by small molecule and antibody, but only aleplasinin has reached Phase 1. The main concern is bleeding risk, given congenital deficiency and the listed liabilities. I would consider it a good candidate if the safety window can be managed.
key_uncertainties: Bleeding risk with chronic PAI-1 inhibition in older people
The GrimAge link is a DNAm surrogate, not measured protein, and the schizophrenia effect was explained by smoking
Whether the Phase 1 drug has shown efficacy or been discontinued
Causal role in human ageing beyond the Amish loss-of-function observation
